utterances.text: You said that the proposal came from the municipal level. Would you please clarify. Did you mean the Municipal Assembly, when you talked about the municipal level, or the municipal boards of political parties?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular statutory provision was something that we inherited from the former Yugoslav law, and it was made part of the relevant law of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina after the first multiparty elections, after we had had a single-party system for a number of years, the Communist League was the one party in question, and they nominated and appointed such individuals. So after this period of time, we moved to a multiparty system. However, we still had the former -- the old laws were still applicable. And as far as I can remember, according to that procedure, it was the president of the municipality who nominated, who proposed, the candidate for this post, and this candidate was then approved by the minister. However, both in the previous system and later on, it became clear that since the minister is not familiar with the reality throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina, and since he could not have known all of the relevant individuals, it was always the proposal of the president of the municipality that was eventually approved. So that was the procedure that was followed at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would not agree with me, would you, if I put it to you that all the proposals, all the nominations in connection with the SUP or what later became MUP, were coming from the SUP or MUP themselves and not from the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The nominations for the chief of police at the local level were always proposals of the social and political community at that level. They were not proposals of the relevant police station, that is, the public security stations. Its employees never made such proposals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As for what concerns the secretariat for national defence, are you referring to the electoral procedure? Were the relevant republican organs in charge of nominations to regional and subregional institutions? So aside from the secretariat of national defence, the public auditing service, post, and telecommunications, railways, the railway, insurance, regional funds, are you familiar with the procedure of appointing candidates to these positions?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the secretary of national defence, I know for sure that the proposal must be processed by the Municipal Assembly. So the Municipal Assembly makes a proposal. I think also the regional secretariat of national defence plays a certain role. I think it provides Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. an opinion, but the republican minister must formally endorse the appointment. But as with the head, this is more -- the character of this appointment is more for many l but what really counts is the proposal which comes from the Municipal Assembly which was adopted most of the times. As for the other institutions you've mentioned, they are all public, that is, state institutions. The Municipal Assembly nominated not the managers of these companies, but the so-called Executive Boards for these public companies. For example, the regional fund had an Executive Board consisting of -- I'm not sure -- 12 or 15 members. I know that the Executive Board of the Prijednabanka [phoen] included 15 members. And members of this Executive Board were nominated by the Municipal Assembly, and this board appointed -- elected its own president. And then this body nominated and appointed managers of all these institutions. The municipality has jurisdiction over these public companies, some of these public companies such as the post and telecommunications or water management, and also the public auditing service as far as I can remember, as they had a republican infrastructure, their hierarchy descending from the republican to the local level, according to the same principle as the positions I have mentioned before, the chief of the local police and the secretary of national defence. There were formal appointments by republican -- from the republican level. But the proposal was made at the local level, which, in practice, meant that all these positions and the candidates were nominated and appointed at the local level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we please have a break now until 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. And you may continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Mujadzic, we spoke about the procedure of appointing persons to leading positions in a number of institutions. Did the Municipal Assembly have a say also when leaders of institutions were replaced or dismissed, where you say that the Municipal Assembly did have a say and did take part in appointing these persons?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Municipal Assembly had the right to give initiative for the replacement of these persons or the dismissal of these persons. And if such requests were justified, they were usually adopted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is a government an organ of legislative or executive authority or power?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Once again, please refrain from theoretical questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The government is by definition an organ of executive power. I'm sorry if I was not supposed to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Your Honour, I think that the witness knows about the structure of the municipal bodies, so yesterday he spoke about these issues. And I just want to clarify, to put some institutions and governmental institutions in a certain fields. So I think that the witness can help us to clarify those issues which have been mentioned previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If it comes to concrete facts, there's no problem. But please read your question, and then you will see immediately that we are, of course, please understand my language correctly, that we are not in a seminar on public international law for beginners.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Prijedor Municipal Assembly, is it an organ of legislative or executive power?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Municipal Assembly takes decisions at the local level. It does not pass laws. The legislative power lies at the state or republican level of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And the municipal level merely took decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Municipal Assembly can -- only has the authority to pass and adopt bylaws?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which organ of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly has the executive power?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Executive Board, the local government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did the Executive Board answer to for its work, the president of the municipality or the members of the municipal board?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your testimony today is that the Executive Board answers to the president of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president is, by definition, at the same time a member of the Municipal Assembly, so if the Executive Board answers to the Municipal Assembly, it should only be logical that it also answers to the president of that body. And this is precisely defined in the municipal statute, the fact that the Executive Board should also answer to the president of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this responsibility of the Executive Board to the president of the Municipal Assembly in his role as a member of the Municipal Assembly, or are there cases when this responsibility is to the president of the Municipal Assembly as an autonomous organ or body?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I'm not an expert in law, so I'm unable to answer this question. But as far as I know from my general political education, is that there are certain issues for which the Executive Board answers directly to the president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with the competences and functions of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its competences and functions are enumerated in the statute of the Municipal Assembly. They are defined under the law on local government at the republican level, and also defined under some constitutional provisions. But I'm not in a position now to enumerate all these competences and functions because essentially I was never a member of the administration. I always worked as a physician, so I'm not familiar with professional details concerning the competences of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When we spoke about the employment office and about the public auditing service about the telecommunications service, water management, and electricity management, Yugoslav railway, do you know whether these Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. institutions were financed from the municipal budget, or in a different way?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Could I ask that the question just clarify the time period that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: First of all, the time period, and we had it already several times in the past, we should not discuss in length what should have been under the law or under the statute, but we have to discuss and find out what have been the facts. And as the counsel of the OTP correctly stated, the period of time is of utmost importance here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry, is Your Honour getting an interpretation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No. Are there problems in the booth?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were talking about the power distribution company, the employment office, and the Yugoslav railways. Was anything else mentioned in addition to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The public auditing service.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as these institutions are concerned, the way they were financed was very different. They didn't have a unified system. The SDK is a state institution only. The employment office is also a state institution. And the power distribution company and the Yugoslav railway and the PTT are profit-oriented institutions. The Yugoslav railway sells tickets and makes money. The PTT takes money for its services, whereas the SDK and the employment office are, in a way, nonprofit organisations. Their task was to organise certain areas for the state to function. Under normal circumstances, these services were financed from the budget.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which budget, the municipal budget or another budget?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two institutions that I have singled out, the state institutions, were financed from the republican budget. But let us not forget that the municipal influence, what we talked about when we talked about the different services, it drew its influence from the fact that these institutions were in the municipal territory, and from the fact that the taxes came from the municipal area. It drew its authority, which we have not tried to dispute, from this very fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday's transcript, page 51, line 8, you contend "the Executive Board is a kind of local government which doesn't have the authority to adopt any significant decision without approval from the Municipal Assembly or from the president of the Municipal Assembly." Would you be so kind --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind and quote the entire sentence. As it is stated: "In normal peacetime, the Executive Board is..." And going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, page 51, line 8: "In normal peacetime, the Executive Board is a kind of local government..."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said "local authority."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Local government.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can read in English so the translator may translate properly in B/C/S, but I may not be that skillful.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the interpreters do not have the transcript, so we can only quote from memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll read from the transcript, so they can translate properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In normal peacetime, the executive committee is a kind of local government which cannot reach any significant decision without the assembly or the president of the municipality having to approve -- issue his approval in respect of this decision." [Interpretation] Can you please tell me and the Trial Chamber which legal or bi-legal provision it was, where you found the foundation for such a statement?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At all levels, starting at the state level, whoever knows anything about the way a state functions know that the government makes proposals for laws. At first, they draft laws. That's the way things were done in the assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Then certain amendments are made. The government then processes these amendments, makes a proposal for the law, which is then discussed again by the assembly, reviewed again by the assembly. And it is only then that a law can be passed. A similar procedure, except not with regard to laws but other sorts of decisions, was applied at the level of local governments. Therefore, the executive committee prepared, as any other administration involved in similar processes, and all the decisions were discussed by the local parliament and either approved or amended, and adopted. This is standard procedure. It is clearly defined in all democratic countries of the world.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you said this, you meant the passing of laws and bylaws, and not just any other affair conducted by the Municipal Assembly which did have other functions, too?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I clearly stated "important decisions." I could not precisely define the statute of the municipality based on the law on local government which precisely defines which decisions exactly. But we are talking about most of the important decisions. It is quite clear that some of the decisions or less important solutions can be made by the Executive Board. But in practice, even with such less important decisions, the Executive Board always consults the president of the Municipal Assembly because at the end of the day, it was the president of the assembly, as any president that could bring up the question of dismissing the representative of the government as well as the president of the Executive Board, who was directly responsible to him for his work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When speaking about the president of the municipality, did he have the power to decide, as an individual, on anything within the competence of the Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about peacetime functioning of the government. The president of the Executive Board, in the intervals between two assembly sessions, looked after the consistent implementation of the assembly's decisions. As far as I know, that was his main function. So all those decisions that were passed and placed within the competence of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Executive Board, that was in charge of implementing them, the duty of the president is to see to it that these decisions are consistently implemented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Municipal Assembly have any part in the work of the secretariat or the inspection teams that were part of the Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to local ministries? Can you just clarify it, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, they were called secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that sounds a bit unclear, because what they actually were, they were local ministries, small local ministries. We can call them that. So the question was whether the Municipal Assembly had any part in their work, in the work of these secretariats?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether it had the authority to order anything. I can give you examples. I have provided examples for other witnesses. Could the Municipal Assembly order the secretary for urban planning and communal services to issue a building permit to anyone, or did this segment of the Executive Board have independence in its activities?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honours. I must repeat again. By profession, I am a doctor, and my knowledge of state administration is limited to my general knowledge of political administration. But I will still try to answer this question. Orders are given in the army, so a general, for example, can issue an order to his subordinates. But in democratic procedure, civilian authorities, if a proposal is made for making a change in the urban plan or resolving any important issues concerning urban planning, since that's what we're talking about, the proposal must be processed and considered by the assembly, and the president of the assembly then sees to it that the decision is consistently implemented. So if a particular local minister or secretary fails to implement a decision in such a way as was decided by the assembly, then the president of the government is the first who is held responsible if his minister does not do his work in a proper way. And then he can start the initiative for such a person, such a man, to be removed from office, because his activity is contrary to the function of his office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can such an initiative be given by any of the deputies at the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a provision in law to that effect. All deputies can initiate such an act.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, are there any decisions taken by the Executive Board which need the approval of the president of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I explained the functioning of the Municipal Assembly and its president on several occasions during my testimony in response to a couple of your questions, but I will try briefly once again --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can perhaps quote your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In yesterday's transcript, on page 51, line 41, you stated the following --

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpretation 14, not 41.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll quote your words in English, and you will have them interpreted. "The Municipal Assembly or the president of the Municipal Assembly is superior to the president of the Executive Board." [Interpretation] You must understand the significance of this question. It is closely related to the issue of responsibility of Dr. Stakic. Sometimes, we really have to be persistent. In this case, we do need explanation and your assistance. This type of superior authority, was it vested only with the Municipal Assembly or with the president himself? Was he also superior to the Executive Board, to the best of your knowledge again?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. To the best of my knowledge, I will try and explain to Their Honours and yourself this issue. And I understand how important it is. I think that the statute of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly would help in this case, or any other statute of the Municipal Assembly which clearly specifies the authority, the duties, and competences of the president and the Municipal Assembly. Since we do not have such a document here, I will briefly try to explain the nature of this relationship.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Chamber has -- does have the statute. Can we agree that the overall authority of the president of the Municipal Assembly is prescribed in the statute, or is there any form of authority that falls outside the scope of the statute? If there's anything that falls outside the framework of the statute, please tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me about the difference of how it was in practice? The president of the municipality is the president of the local parliament. And he is in charge of presiding over the local parliament, which, in turn, is in charge of issuing proposals, adopting proposals, issuing initiatives with respect to local decisions which are provided for by the Executive Board in form of proposals. And it is the president who, later on, makes sure that the decisions taken by the local parliament are implemented through the executive body, which is the local government together with its president. So it is the president who makes sure that the decisions are implemented by the executive body. So for the implementation of -- it is the president of the municipality who is responsible for the implementation of these decisions, because not every deputy can be involved in this. Being a deputy is a local, nonprofessional function. Therefore, it is the duty of the president, who is employed as such and who receives salary for this type of office, who is in charge of supervising this implementation. Practically speaking, his role is much greater than the role of a simple deputy to the assembly. His influence, of course, is greater than the influence of the deputies. There is a big difference between being a deputy to the assembly and its president. Formally speaking, they are at the same level. However, in practical terms, the president of the municipality, in accordance with its statute, has greater responsibility, influence, and de facto authority than the deputies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The decisions reached by the Municipal Assembly, can they be adopted only through the voting of its members, that is, the deputies to the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The statute also makes provision for that. A certain Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. majority is stipulated. It is referred to as a quorum. Then depending on the nature of the decision, a two-third majority quorum is necessary or a simple majority, as it is usually the case in most of the local governments in democratic countries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The chief of the public security station, Mr. Talundzic, before the war, was he responsible for his work to the municipal structures of government, or was he answerable to the competent and superior bodies within the MUP itself by virtue of relevant statutory provisions?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally and legally speaking, the chief of the local police is answerable in terms of hierarchy to the chief of the regional police who, in turn, is answerable to the chief of the police at the level of the republic, that is, the minister of the interior. However, as I have already explained, in the case of the appointment procedure for the local chief of police and as it is the local level of government who is responsible for his appointment, then practically speaking, in reality, the chief of local police is answerable to the local authorities. Because it is the local authority who, at any point in time, could dismiss him or initiate his removal which, again, in practice, was always adopted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What body of local authority are you talking about when you said about its being able to initiate the removal of Mr. Hasan Talundzic, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, in practice, this was always the president of the municipality, the individual who had the highest ranking position in a given socio-political community. And when I say a socio-political community, I am referring to the municipality. The term comes from the former terminology of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia. Some of the terms have changed because of the nature of these positions and structures changed. The municipal structure changed in Bosnia and Herzegovina after the cantons had been introduced, so I have to apologise for using the term "a socio-political community," however, this was the term that was used before. And it referred to a higher level of local authority than is the case with the local community in European countries. So we're not talking about the same level of authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did it work in practice? Would the president of the municipality just write a letter, call someone by telephone, and ask for such a removal or dismissal?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In practice, it was usually enough to have a telephone conversation with the minister. And the minister would then adopt a decision on the removal of the local chief of police. So in practice, the problem could be solved in this manner. The president of the municipality could -- now I'm not quite sure what body I'm talking about -- could formally initiate the removal of the chief of police for various reasons. But in practice, it was often enough to have an informal conversation with the minister in order to have the local chief of police replaced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it your testimony today that there was a legal basis and legal authority and competence of the president of the municipality to take part in the procedure of removal of the local chief of police? I'm referring to the municipal police structures.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, speaking of Talundzic's appointment specifically, I think that there were seven proposals that were sent to the minister. I don't remember the exact number at this point. I'm not sure about the body, the local body, from which these proposals emanated. I cannot speak about that with certainty. However, I am certain that it is the president of the municipality who wields the greatest influence in this respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The president of the municipality, did he have any influence to -- on the JNA and the appointment of JNA officers?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the period of time before 1990, to the peacetime?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In that case, no, he didn't have any influence on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cehajic, in his capacity of the president of the municipality, could he issue orders to Mr. Hasan Talundzic as the chief of public security station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to formal, legal orders, or informal orders?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the formal ones.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally speaking, the president of the municipality cannot formally issue orders to anyone in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking of informal influence, we all know that it is always the wife of the individual who has the greatest influence on him. However, let us concentrate on the civilian authorities and informal orders.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no such informal orders, unless we're talking about dictatorship.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Muhamed Cehajic, as the president of the Municipal Assembly and the president of the National Defence Council, referring to the period of time prior to the 30th of April, 1992, could he issue any orders to the military, to, for instance, Zeljaja or Arsic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he could not. He didn't have either formal or informal influence, in that respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cehajic as the president of the Municipal Assembly and the president of the National Defence Council, could he nominate or appoint anyone to the positions within the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did have some influence over the Territorial Defence, because the Territorial Defence commanders were appointed on the basis of the nominations made by the local, that is, the municipal parliament. I think I've already explained that, that the commander at the level of the republic was appointed pursuant to a nomination which came from the local, municipal level. So he did have some influence over that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 33, line 14 of Monday's transcript, I'll read in English so that you can receive accurate interpretation. You stated the following: [In English] "... Was designed to function in immediate threat of war, and, of course, in war danger. By virtue of that function, the president of that council is also the president of the municipality, and he is also the civilian commander of the defence of the town. And according to law, he's responsible for the defence of the town on the local level. So both the chief of police and the commander of the civilian protection and the defence, Territorial Defence, are all under his authority. And also, in terms of, not really immediate, common subordination, but in a certain sense, he was also the superior of the army that was in the area." [Interpretation] Will you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I said -- at least, I don't remember having said that he was superior to the military stationed in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we can clear it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I just -- the transcript did not pick up the beginning of the quote, so I'm not a hundred per cent sure. Perhaps it was interpreted into B/C/S, but the beginning of the quote where he indicated that it was the National Defence Council that we were talking about was not included in the transcript. So I'm not sure if the witness knows the body that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] I wasn't aware of this mistake, so the sentence starts with "the council for national security was designed... ," so the rest we have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we can correct your testimony today, if you believe that you did not state that he was superior to the army. We can perhaps clarify.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about the National Defence Council, which is provided for in the relevant law of the republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and if we are talking about the circumstances that I described and indicated, that is, the normal circumstances, then I don't remember having said that the body in question was superior to the army. I don't think I can talk about any superior authority of the local government over the military. However, there was a certain coordination, because the commander -- the commanders who were located, stationed, in the area could attend the sessions of the councils. And the law also provided for the fact that, aside from the chief of police, the commander of the Territorial Defence, the vice-president of the Executive Board, who is also at the same time the commander of the civil defence, that other members can also be appointed. This does not exclude the possibility for a commander of the military garrisoned in the area, and whose area of responsibilities at the same time the area of combat operations, to be appointed to the National Defence Council at the level of the municipality as its member. So the law provides for that possibility as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, this body is only established in cases of imminent threat of war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a collective body?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, I have to specify that the body can also become operational in some other circumstances. You have mentioned only two of such circumstances, the immediate threat of war and the war itself. However, there are certain circumstances, certain situations where it can also become operational in a given municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking of Municipal Assemblies in general, do they normally have such a body in peacetime? I'm referring to the National Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just explained that. Theoretically speaking, it is possible for this body to be established in peacetime as well. For example, on the territories of some municipalities right after the war, a number of terrorist groups appeared. You probably remember such cases from the media, such terrorist groups were located on the territory of the municipality. And their presence required immediate action. So, it was possible for this body to convene in a situation of that kind or in some other situations where the overall safety of the municipality and the local population was in danger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly did you have in mind when you said that the president of the National Defence Council was also, at the same time, the civilian commander of the defence of the town?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the statute provides that he is responsible for the overall defence of the town and for everything of that nature that is going on in the town, then that makes him the civilian commander of the local defence. It is merely a different description for what I have already indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can this duty also be found in the statute of the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not literally speaking. I have just described it that way, but I don't know whether you are now talking about the wording, the legal wording, itself. I am not a lawyer. I have merely provided you with a description of this concept as a politician, not as a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My mistake. I apologise. I not intend to insist on the title of this office. I just wanted to find out whether these competences and the function itself are provided for in the statute as part of the overall authority of the president of the National Defence Council, either in the statute or some other laws or bylaws?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What specific function do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact that he is superior to the chief of police, to the chief of civilian defence, and the chief of Territorial Defence, and that all are under his command.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we want to be precise, commands and orders are issued, generally speaking, by commanders of military units. The words "command" and "order" are -- belong to the military terminology. In wartime, the civilian commander of the defence of a country is usually the president of the country, or the prime minister, depending on the constitution. And his competences are described as civilian command. But he usually is not in charge of command itself. There's always a number of various bodies in charge of adopting different decisions. They are implemented by the police or the military, and it is the president who takes care, who makes sure that such decisions are implemented. The same goes for the commander of the Territorial Defence. The president of the municipality and the president of this National Defence Council makes sure that these decisions are implemented. So the president of the municipality does have competences -- certain competences over the commander of the military, the chief of police in that sense, also over the commander of the civilian defence, over all members of the National Defence Council. So he is in charge of supervising the implementation of the decisions adopted by this body and other bodies within the municipality. He supervises the implementation of these decisions as the president, in this case, as the president of the National Defence Council. And that makes him responsible for what you have just enumerated, for the various functions that you have indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your testimony today that the chief of police, civilian protection and Territorial Defence, that all of them are under the command of the president of the National Defence Council and that this is provided for by a law?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not what I said. Please don't try to insinuate. I explained very clearly the nature of these relationships which you are now simplifying with a single word and you're trying to insinuate that I said something that I didn't say. If that's what it takes, I will repeat my explanation again or you can just read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that the president of the National Defence Council is not superior to the police, civil protection, and Territorial Defence, and is not their commander? He must be either of these two, or maybe half he is and half he is not. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Wait a minute, please. The objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The question is it has already been asked and answered..

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained. And for clarification, once again, I said on previous occasions, it is not for a witness to tell the Bench what is the law, what should have been in the past. If there would be always no discrepancy between the law and reality, we would never need a court in the world. We have to find out what are the facts, what has been the law, and has there been any discrepancies? And therefore, please, I would ask both parties not to ask questions to a physician on the legal situation what should have been. We can read the statute ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Your Honour, if I may, our client is charged for command and personal, individual responsibility, and also de jure and de facto. If my learned friend from the opposite side is ready to withdraw his indictment in the de jure part, we'll quit asking these questions. And as long as our client is charged de jure, we have to go and ask questions like these. I apologise once again. Another thing, I quoted the part of the statement of this witness. I just wanted to clarify whether what has been mentioned in this transcript is relevant or not. And secondly, is it true or not? Even the witness, by himself, clarified that he never mentioned army as a part of subordinate part under our client's responsibility. I tried further on to clarify whether the TO, civil defence, and police was part of this common responsibility. So I think that my line of questions is crucial and has to be -- these questions have to be asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The point actually is that we have got precise and -- I apologise -- lengthy answers on this issue. And I don't think that it's really helpful to summarise these answers. We will have a look very, very carefully on that what has been said. And it's not necessary to ask for a second answer on the same issue. And this was the point of the objection of the OTP, and therefore, the objection was sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, I would just like to say one sentence regarding the objection by the counsel for the Defence. [In English] I don't have objection. I have a comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's for the parties to put questions here. And please proceed, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Mujadzic, I would like to ask you something about the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor SDA. Did the Crisis Staff of the SDA, of Prijedor municipality, was it founded in October 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly now whether it was October or November. Possibly even 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll allow for that, the fact that you can't remember. But the members, this Crisis Staff, were they Mr. Muhamed Cehajic, yourself, Mr. Becir Medunjanin, Mr. Hilmija Hopovac, Mr. Mustafa Hadzic and Mr. Camil Pezo?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of these people were members of the Crisis Staff, but I'm not sure about all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please help us out and tell us exactly which of the people from this list were members of the Crisis Staff of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Must I answer this question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, I think the witness may prefer closed session. I'm not sure if that's what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any objections against --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: -- Private session? I think it's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stands adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
